correctness.rationale: The primal weights on length-three constant, adjacent-repeat, and other patterns are 1,1/2,1/4; all fifteen equality patterns of length four have coverage at least one. The dual gives mass 1 to aaaa and aabb, 1/[2(q-2)] to abca, and 1/[4(q-2)] to four-distinct words; counting occurrences in each center type gives dual sums exactly one and matching objective q(q+1)^2/4 for all q>=3. Binary explicit primal and dual achieve four. Independent exact Fraction enumeration for q=2,3,4,5,6 checked every distinct deletion set and every dual inequality, with common objectives 4,12,25,45,147/2. For the integer covering I(q,3,1), published s(4,3)>1/3 makes the asymptotic gap liminf at least 4s>4/3; this is a conditional comparison using the published bound, not a calculation of s.

evidence: Pikhurko–Verbitsky–Zhukovskii prove s(r+1,r)>1/r for integer codes. This asymptotic integer theorem, not a matching continuous LP optimum, is used only for the strict gap.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Generic packing-covering LP duality guarantees equality of objectives when feasible primal and dual certificates coincide, but does not derive this novel explicit pair for all alphabet sizes.
